system_prompt:
You are an expert Python programmer. You are given the following problem:\n\n
def split_words(txt):
    '''
    Given a string of words, return a list of words split on whitespace, if no whitespaces exists in the text you

    alphabet, ord('a') = 0, ord('b') = 1, ... ord('z') = 25
    Examples
    split_words("Hello world!") ➞ ["Hello", "world!"]
    split_words("Hello,world!") ➞ ["Hello", "world!"]
    split_words("abcdef") == 3 
    '''

To help with your reasoning, you will be given a Dafny specification, but prioritize the docstring as the Dafny specification could be incorrect. user_prompt:
method split_words(txt: string) returns (result: array<string>)
    requires txt != null
    ensures (forall i: int :: 0 <= i < result.Length ==> result[i] != null) // Ensure no null words in result
    ensures (result.Length > 0 ==> (forall w: string :: w in result ==> w.Trim() != "")) // Ensure no empty words
    ensures (result.Length > 0 ==> (forall w: string :: w in result ==> w != "") || (result.Length == 1 && result[0] == "3")) // Handles case where only lower-case letters count
    ensures (result.Length == 0 ==> (count_lowercase_odd(txt) == 0)) // If no words, count of lowercase letters should be zero
    ensures (result.Length > 0 ==> count_whitespace_split(txt) || count_commas_split(txt) || count_lowercase_odd(txt) > 0) // Ensure at least one condition is met

method count_lowercase_odd(txt: string) returns (count: int)
    requires txt != null
    ensures count >= 0
    ensures count == CountLowercaseOdd(txt)

method count_whitespace_split(txt: string) returns (flag: bool)
    requires txt != null
    ensures flag ==> (txt.Contains(" ") || txt.Contains("\t") || txt.Contains("\n")) // Check for whitespace

method count_commas_split(txt: string) returns (flag: bool)
    requires txt != null
    ensures flag ==> txt.Contains(",") // Check for commas

method CountLowercaseOdd(txt: string) returns (count: int)
    requires txt != null
    ensures count >= 0
    ensures count == CountLowercaseOddInternal(txt)
